title: Battleships in a Board
statement: `board` is an `m x n` grid in which every cell is either `'X'` (a piece of a battleship) or `'.'` (open water). Each battleship is a straight line of `'X'` cells, lying either in one row (`1 x k`) or in one column (`k x 1`), for any length `k >= 1`. Two different battleships never share an edge: between them there is always at least one `'.'` cell horizontally or vertically (touching only at a corner is allowed). Return how many battleships are on the board.
constraints: Every group of edge-connected 'X' cells is a straight 1 x k or k x 1 line
notes:
## Intuition

The general way to count ships is a flood fill: each time you meet an unvisited `'X'`, count a ship and mark all of its connected cells. That needs a visited grid (or changes to `board`) and recursion. The shape rules make it unnecessary. Every ship is a straight line, so it has exactly one first cell in reading order: its top cell if it is vertical, its leftmost cell if it is horizontal. That cell is the only one of the ship with no `'X'` directly above it and no `'X'` directly to its left, so counting such cells counts ships.

## Approach

1. Set `count = 0` and scan every cell by `row` and `col`.
2. Skip the cell if it is `'.'`.
3. Skip it if the cell above (`row - 1`) is `'X'`: it continues a vertical ship that was already counted.
4. Skip it if the cell to the left (`col - 1`) is `'X'`: it continues a horizontal ship.
5. Otherwise this is the first cell of a new ship, so add 1 to `count`.
6. Return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`board` has `'X'` at `(0,0)`, `(0,3)`, `(1,3)` and `(2,3)`.

- `(0,0)`: no cell above or to the left, so `count = 1`.
- `(0,3)`: row 0 has nothing above, and `(0,2)` is `'.'`, so `count = 2`.
- `(1,3)` and `(2,3)`: the cell above each is `'X'`, so they are skipped.

The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · n): each cell is looked at once with two neighbour checks.
- Space: O(1): no visited grid, no recursion and `board` is not modified.

## Pitfalls

- Check the row and column bounds before reading `board[row - 1]` or `board[row][col - 1]`.
- Counting every `'X'` counts cells, not ships.
- Ships may touch diagonally; only the cell directly above and directly to the left matter.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | ships found so far |
| `row`, `col` | the cell being examined |

narration.2: No ships have been found yet.
narration.3: Scan the board row by row...
narration.4: ...and each row from left to right.
narration.5: Open water cannot start a ship.
narration.8: An 'X' above means this cell continues a vertical ship counted earlier.
narration.11: An 'X' to the left means this cell continues a horizontal ship counted earlier.
narration.14: Nothing above or to the left: this is the first cell of a new ship.
narration.17: Each ship was counted exactly once, at its first cell.
